newsitem.title: MEXICO: Results show Mexico ruling PRI lost majority.
newsitem.headline: Results show Mexico ruling PRI lost majority.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has lost its absolute majority in the lower house of Congress, official results from Sunday's mid-term elections showed on Thursday.

The PRI, which has ruled Mexico since 1929, needed to win at least 167 of the 300 directly-elected seats and tally at least 42.2 percent of the popular vote to clinch a majority under Mexico's complicated electoral law.

With 294 of 300 directly-elected seats counted, the PRI had won 159 versus 69 for the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and 65 for the conservative National Action Party (PAN), results showed.
Another 200 seats in the 500-seat body would also be alloted proportionally according to the percentage of the overall vote, the Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) said.
IFE officials said they would complete the vote count in the remaining districts later on Thursday or early Friday.
Preliminary results from 87 percent of the vote counted showed the PRI winning about 39 percent of the total vote compared to 27 percent for the PAN and 25.60 percent for the PRD.
